extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners on when and how to make, withdraw, or justify rejections (including final rejections), disclaimers, res judicata rejections, reissue-related rejections, and rejections of previously allowed claims; includes required form paragraphs and procedural limits. Covers first, second, and subsequent actions, IDS effects, and special situations (continuations, RCEs, reexaminations, joint research exclusions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral when earlier foreign application exists (35 U.S.C. 185 potential)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner learns of the existence of a corresponding foreign application which appears to have been filed before the United States application had been on file for 6 months, and if the invention apparently was made in this country, he or she shall refer the application to Licensing and Review Section of Technology Center (TC) work group 3640, calling attention to the foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pending investigation of the possible violation, the application may be returned to the TC for prosecution on the merits. When otherwise in condition for allowance, the application will be again submitted to Licensing and Review Section of TC work group 3640 unless the latter has already reported that the foreign filing involves no bar to the United States application. If necessary to take action under 35 U.S.C. 185, Licensing and Review Section of TC work group 3640 will request transfer of the application to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer as ground for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be rejected on the ground that applicant has disclaimed the subject matter involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disclaimer may arise, for example, from the applicant’s failure to: (A) make claims suggested for interference with another application under 37 CFR 41.202(c); (B) copy a claim from a patent when suggested by the examiner; or (C) respond or appeal, within the time limit fixed, to the examiner’s rejection of claims copied from a patent. The rejection on disclaimer applies to all claims not patentably distinct from the disclaimed subject matter as well as to the claims directly involved. Rejections based on disclaimer should be made by using one of Form Paragraphs 7.48 and 7.49.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.48 — Failure To Present Claims for Interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. [2] based upon claim [3] of Patent No. [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to present claims and/or take necessary steps for interference purposes after notification that interfering subject matter is claimed constitutes a disclaimer of the subject matter. Use only after applicant notified that interference must be instituted and applicant refused to copy the claims. In bracket 2 insert --102(g)-- or --102(g)/103(a)--. In bracket 4 insert the patent number and --in view of _____-- if another reference also relied upon. When rejection is under 35 U.S.C. 103(a), include the examiner's basis for a finding of obviousness. Note that interferences may include obvious variants (see MPEP Chapter 2300).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.49 — Rejection, Disclaimer, Failure To Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An adverse judgment against claim [1] has been entered by the Board. Claim [2] stand(s) finally disposed of for failure to reply to or appeal from the examiner’s rejection of such claim(s) presented for interference within the time for appeal or civil action specified in 37 CFR 1.304.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An adverse judgment against a claim is a final action of the Office requiring no further action by the Office to dispose of the claim permanently. See 37 CFR 41.127(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Res judicata as ground for rejection — limits and application
rubrics_metrics.description: Res judicata may constitute a proper ground for rejection, but it should be applied only when the earlier decision was a decision of the Board of Appeals or any one of the reviewing courts and when there is no opportunity for further court review of the earlier decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of a second application copending with an earlier application does not preclude the use of res judicata as a ground of rejection for the second application claims. When making a rejection on res judicata, action should ordinarily be made also on the basis of prior art, especially in continuing applications. The same prior art relied upon in the earlier decision would often again be applicable. The MPEP cites case law examples where res judicata rejections were sustained and cases where they were reversed; apply cautiously in light of precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application scope limitation (35 U.S.C. 251)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 251 forbids the granting of a reissue 'enlarging the scope of the claims of the original patent' unless the reissue is applied for within 2 years from the grant of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition is absolute and applies to any claim broader in any respect than the claims of the original patent; such claims may be rejected as being barred by 35 U.S.C. 251. However, when the reissue is applied for within 2 years (or properly claims the benefit of a broadening reissue application filed within 2 years of the patent grant), the examiner does not go into the question of undue delay. The same section permits filing of a reissue by the assignee of the entire interest only where it does not enlarge scope. A defective reissue oath is a ground for rejecting all claims in the reissue application (see MPEP § 1444). Note that a reissue application is 'special' and remains so even if applicant does not make a prompt reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of previously allowed claims — supervisory approval and deference
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable shall thereafter be rejected only after the proposed rejection has been submitted to the primary examiner for consideration of all the facts and approval of the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great care should be exercised in authorizing such a rejection. Full faith and credit should be given to the search and action of a previous examiner unless there is a clear error in the previous action or knowledge of other prior art. In general, an examiner should not take an entirely new approach or make a new search in the mere hope of finding something. When rejecting a previously allowed claim due to newly discovered art, use Form Paragraph 7.50 and the action requires the signature of a Primary Examiner (MPEP § 1004).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.50 — Claims Previously Allowed, Now Rejected, New Art
rubrics_metrics.description: The indicated allowability of claim [1] is withdrawn in view of the newly discovered reference(s) to [2]. Rejection(s) based on the newly cited reference(s) follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 insert the name(s) of the newly discovered reference. Any action including this form paragraph requires the signature of a Primary Examiner (MPEP § 1004).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection after allowance of application
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on a reference after allowance is governed by MPEP § 1308.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1308.01 for procedures and limits when a reference is discovered after allowance that may warrant rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection general rule (37 CFR 1.113) — when permitted and reply limits
rubrics_metrics.description: On the second or any subsequent examination or consideration by the examiner the rejection or other action may be made final, whereupon applicant's reply is limited to appeal, or to amendment as specified in § 1.114 or § 1.116; petitions may be taken for objections/requirements not involved in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In making such final rejection, the examiner shall repeat or state all grounds of rejection then considered applicable to the claims, clearly stating the reasons in support thereof. Reply to a final rejection must include cancellation of, or appeal from, the rejection of each rejected claim. Before final rejection is in order a clear issue should be developed between examiner and applicant: thoroughly search and apply references in the first action, and the applicant should amend with a view to avoiding all grounds of rejection and objection. Avoid switching subject matter or shifting to different sets of references in successive actions as this defeats early termination. The examiner should not issue hasty and ill-considered final rejections; the applicant is entitled to a full and fair hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of grounds requirement in final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: In making the final rejection, all outstanding grounds of rejection of record should be carefully reviewed, and any such grounds relied on in the final rejection should be reiterated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They must be clearly developed so the applicant may readily judge the advisability of an appeal, unless a single previous Office action contains a complete statement supporting the rejection. Where a single previous Office action contains a complete statement, the final rejection may refer to such a statement and should include a rebuttal of any arguments raised in the applicant’s reply. The final rejection letter should conclude with Form Paragraph 7.39.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.39 and 7.39.01 — final action wording and applicant options
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.39: 'THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.' Applicant is reminded of the extension of time policy as set forth in 37 CFR 1.136(a). ¶7.39.01: explains options after final rejection (appeal or limited amendment) and filing requirements for Notice of Appeal and appeal fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shortened statutory period for reply to this final action is set to expire THREE MONTHS from the mailing date; if a first reply is filed within TWO MONTHS and advisory action mailed after the three-month period, the shortened period expires on the date the advisory action is mailed; in no event will the statutory period expire later than SIX MONTHS from mailing date. Form paragraph 7.39 should not be used in reissue litigation cases or reexamination proceedings (examiner notes). 7.39.01 clarifies that an amendment after final cannot be made as a matter of right unless it merely cancels claims or complies with earlier formal requirements; amendments touching merits may be admitted only upon showing good and sufficient reasons why necessary and why not presented earlier. Failure to file Notice of Appeal properly within the period for reply (or obtain extension) will result in abandonment. The Office Action Summary Form PTOL-326 should be used in all Office actions up to and including final rejections. See MPEP §§ 714.12 and 714.13 for amendments after final rejection and §2271 for final rejection practice in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: When final rejection is proper on second or subsequent action
rubrics_metrics.description: Under present practice, second or any subsequent actions on the merits shall be final, except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant’s amendment of the claims, nor based on information submitted in an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where information is submitted in an IDS during the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee, the examiner may use the information and make the next Office action final whether or not the claims have been amended, provided no other new ground of rejection not necessitated by amendment is introduced. If information is submitted in reply to a requirement under 37 CFR 1.105, the examiner may NOT make the next Office action final unless all instances of application of such art are necessitated by amendment. A second/subsequent action should not be made final if it includes a rejection, on prior art not of record, of any claim amended to include limitations which should reasonably have been expected to be claimed. An examiner cannot be expected to anticipate applicant amendments except in limited circumstances (e.g., where examiner suggests how applicant can overcome a 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of amendments to 35 U.S.C. 102(e) and special disqualification situations
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or any subsequent action may not be made final if it contains a new ground of rejection necessitated by amendments to 35 U.S.C. 102(e) by the 2002 Technical Amendments Act, unless the new ground was necessitated by an amendment to the claims or as a result of information submitted in an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97(c) with fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying any 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 references, the examiner should anticipate that a statement averring common ownership at the time the invention was made may disqualify any patent or application applied in a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 based on 102(e). If such a statement is filed in reply and claims are not amended, the examiner may not make the next Office action final if a new rejection is made. If a reference is disqualified under the joint research agreement provision of 35 U.S.C. 103(c) and a new double patenting rejection based upon the disqualified reference is applied, the next Office action containing the new double patenting rejection may be made final even if applicant did not amend the claims (provided the examiner introduces no other new ground of rejection not necessitated by amendment or an IDS filed during the specified period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against allowing amended claims where patentable novelty not pointed out
rubrics_metrics.description: In the consideration of claims in an amended case where no attempt is made to point out the patentable novelty, the examiner should be on guard not to allow such claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claims may be finally rejected if, in the opinion of the examiner, they are clearly open to rejection on grounds of record. See MPEP § 714.04 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.40 and its variants — final due to amendment or IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.40: 'Applicant’s amendment necessitated the new ground(s) of rejection presented in this Office action. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 7.40 where an action is made final including new grounds of rejection necessitated by applicant’s amendment. 7.40.01 notes IDS with fee prompted new ground(s) (see MPEP § 609.04(b)). 7.40.02 covers invoking the joint research agreement prior art exclusion under 35 U.S.C. 103(c). Each variant reminds applicant of extension of time policy and carries the same shortened statutory period language. Examiner notes indicate these paragraphs should not be used where other new grounds are introduced that were not necessitated by amendment or an IDS with fee; include bracket insertions for dates where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection on first action — when proper (continuations, RCEs, CPAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of a new application may be finally rejected in the first Office action where (A) the new application is a continuing application of, or a substitute for, an earlier application, and (B) all claims are drawn to the same invention claimed in the earlier application and would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of an application for which an RCE has been filed may be finally rejected in the action immediately subsequent to the filing of the RCE where all claims after entry of submission under 37 CFR 1.114 are drawn to the same invention and would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered earlier. A first Office action in a continuation, substitute application, or RCE may not be made final if it contains material that was presented in the earlier application after final rejection or closing of prosecution but denied entry because new issues were raised or new matter was involved, or if a continuation-in-part includes new subject matter not present in the earlier application. A request for interview prior to first action on a continuing or substitute application should ordinarily be granted. Use Form Paragraphs 7.41, 7.41.03, or 7.42.09 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection prematureness — raising and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Any question as to prematureness of a final rejection should be raised while the application is still pending before the primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prematureness is a question of practice, distinct from tenability of the rejection. It may not be advanced as a ground for appeal or complaint before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences; it is reviewable by petition under 37 CFR 1.181 (see MPEP § 1002.02(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of finality of a final rejection (premature)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on request by applicant for reconsideration, the primary examiner finds the final rejection to have been premature, he or she should withdraw the finality of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The finality must be withdrawn while the application is still pending; the examiner cannot withdraw the final rejection once the application is abandoned. Once the finality has been withdrawn, the next Office action may be made final if the conditions set forth in MPEP § 706.07(a) are met. Use Form Paragraph 7.42 when withdrawing finality of the last Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of final rejection after entry — limits and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered, it should not be withdrawn at applicant's request except on a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further amendment or argument will be considered in certain instances; an amendment placing the application in condition for allowance or better for appeal may be admitted. The examiner may withdraw the rejection of finally rejected claims if new facts or reasons are presented convincing the examiner the previously rejected claims are allowable or patentable (in reexamination), or to apply a new ground of rejection. Withdrawing a final rejection to enter a new ground should be limited to situations where a new reference either fully meets at least one claim or meets it except for differences shown to be completely obvious. The practice should not be used for subsidiary, cumulative, or merely better references. When a final rejection is withdrawn, all amendments filed after the final rejection are ordinarily entered. New grounds of rejection made in an Office action reopening prosecution after filing an appeal brief require approval of the supervisory patent examiner (see MPEP § 1002.02(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for reply to final rejection (shortened statutory period principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period for reply to a final action is typically set (for example, three months) and various form paragraphs describe the interplay of filing a first reply within two months, advisory actions, and the maximum statutory period (six months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs (e.g., 7.39, 7.40 variants) contain standard language describing the shortened statutory period set to expire THREE MONTHS from the mailing date, the effect of a first reply filed within TWO MONTHS when an advisory action is delayed, and the maximum statutory period of SIX MONTHS. Examiner notes specify exceptions for reissue litigation cases and reexamination proceedings with different shortened statutory periods (SSP). See 37 CFR 1.136(a) and related MPEP sections for full details.
